To commemorate the divine massacre of the Egyptian children, God instructs the Israelites to "sacrifice to the Lord all that openeth the matrix" -- all the males, that is. God has no use for dead, burnt female bodies.

How many days is unleavened bread to be eaten during the passover?

God avoids leading the Israelites through "the land of the Philistines" hundreds of years before the Philistines were established in Canaan.

items.html: If a thief be found breaking up, and be smitten that he die, there shall no blood be shed for him.

blocks.html: If a thief is caught breaking in and is killed, the person who kills him shall not be punished if it happened at night.

items.html: If the sun be risen upon him, there shall be blood shed for him; for he should make full restitution; if he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.

blocks.html:
But if it happened in the daytime, the person who killed the thief shall be killed.

If a thief is caught and is too poor to make a complete restitution, then he is to be sold to pay for his theft. [2]

items.html: If a man shall cause a field or vineyard to be eaten, and shall put in his beast, and shall feed in another man's field; of the best of his own field, and of the best of his own vineyard, shall he make restitution.
If fire break out, and catch in thorns, so that the stacks of corn, or the standing corn, or the field, be consumed therewith; he that kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.
If a man shall deliver unto his neighbour money or stuff to keep, and it be stolen out of the man's house; if the thief be found, let him pay double.
If the thief be not found, then the master of the house shall be brought unto the judges, to see whether he have put his hand unto his neighbour's goods.

For all manner of trespass, whether it be for ox, for ass, for sheep, for raiment, or for any manner of lost thing which another challengeth to be his, the cause of both parties shall come before the judges; and whom the judges shall condemn, he shall pay double unto his neighbour.
If a man deliver unto his neighbour an ass, or an ox, or a sheep, or any beast, to keep; and it die, or be hurt, or driven away, no man seeing it:
Then shall an oath of the LORD be between them both, that he hath not put his hand unto his neighbour's goods; and the owner of it shall accept thereof, and he shall not make it good.
And if it be stolen from him, he shall make restitution unto the owner thereof.
If it be torn in pieces, then let him bring it for witness, and he shall not make good that which was torn.
And if a man borrow ought of his neighbour, and it be hurt, or die, the owner thereof being not with it, he shall surely make it good.
But if the owner thereof be with it, he shall not make it good: if it be an hired thing, it came for his hire.

items.html: And in the candlesticks shall be four bowls made like unto almonds, with their knops and their flowers.

blocks.html: Put four almond-like bowls in the candlesticks, with knops and flowers.

items.html: And there shall be a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, according to the six branches that proceed out of the candlestick.
Their knops and their branches shall be of the same: all it shall be one beaten work of pure gold.

blocks.html: Under each pair of the branches put a knop of pure gold.

items.html: And thou shalt make the seven lamps thereof: and they shall light the lamps thereof, that they may give light over against it.
And the tongs thereof, and the snuffdishes thereof, shall be of pure gold.

blocks.html: Make seven lamps, with tongs and snuffdishes of pure gold.

items.html: Of a talent of pure gold shall he make it, with all these vessels.
And look that thou make them after their pattern, which was shewed thee in the mount.

blocks.html: Use a talent of pure gold for the vessels, and make them according to the instructions I gave you on the mount.

footnotes.html:
The LORD spake unto Moses, saying.... (v.1)

God wastes most of the last 16 chapters of Exodus on instructions for making tables, curtains, candlesticks, snuffers, girdles, bonnets, perfumes, etc. This stuff is so important that much of it is repeated. As a result, the last 40% of Exodus is one of the most boring sections in the Bible.

Thou shalt make two cherubims of gold. (v.18)

God tells Moses to make some graven images for him, contrary to the commandment given in Ex 20:4and Dt 5:8.

Is it OK to make graven images?

blocks.html: God's instructions for making curtains
26:1-37, Cf. 1

items.html: Moreover thou shalt make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet: with cherubims of cunning work shalt thou make them.
The length of one curtain shall be eight and twenty cubits, and the breadth of one curtain four cubits: and every one of the curtains shall have one measure.
The five curtains shall be coupled together one to another; and other five curtains shall be coupled one to another.

blocks.html:
God continues his instructions to Moses, saying,

Make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine linen, blue, purple, and scarlet.

Include cherubim of cunning work. [2]

Make each curtain 28 cubits long.

Make two big curtains out of the ten by joining two groups of five curtains.

items.html: And thou shalt make loops of blue upon the edge of the one curtain from the selvedge in the coupling; and likewise shalt thou make in the uttermost edge of another curtain, in the coupling of the second.
Fifty loops shalt thou make in the one curtain, and fifty loops shalt thou make in the edge of the curtain that is in the coupling of the second; that the loops may take hold one of another.

blocks.html: Make fifty blue loops on the tops of the curtains.

items.html: And thou shalt make fifty taches of gold, and couple the curtains together with the taches: and it shall be one tabernacle.

blocks.html: Make fifty gold taches and join the curtains together with them.

items.html: And thou shalt make curtains of goats' hair to be a covering upon the tabernacle: eleven curtains shalt thou make.
The length of one curtain shall be thirty cubits, and the breadth of one curtain four cubits: and the eleven curtains shall be all of one measure.

blocks.html: Make eleven goat hair curtains to cover the tabernacle, each curtain shall be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide.

items.html: And thou shalt couple five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves, and shalt double the sixth curtain in the forefront of the tabernacle.

blocks.html: Make two big goat hair curtains by joining two six in one curtain and five in the other.

items.html: And thou shalt make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain that is outmost in the coupling, and fifty loops in the edge of the curtain which coupleth the second.

blocks.html: Make fifty loops on the edge of each big goats' hair curtain.

items.html: And thou shalt make fifty taches of brass, and put the taches into the loops, and couple the tent together, that it may be one.

blocks.html: Make fifty taches of brass. Tie the tent together by putting the taches in the loops.

items.html: And the remnant that remaineth of the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that remaineth, shall hang over the backside of the tabernacle.

And a cubit on the one side, and a cubit on the other side of that which remaineth in the length of the curtains of the tent, it shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle on this side and on that side, to cover it.

blocks.html: Hang any remaining curtains over the backside of the tabernacle, with a cubit on each side.

items.html: And thou shalt make a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering above of badgers' skins.

blocks.html: Make a tent covering from ram skins dyed red, and another covering from badger skins.

items.html: And thou shalt make boards for the tabernacle of shittim wood standing up.
Ten cubits shall be the length of a board, and a cubit and a half shall be the breadth of one board.

blocks.html: Make boards out of shittim wood, 10 cubits long and 1.5 cubits wide.

items.html: Two tenons shall there be in one board, set in order one against another: thus shalt thou make for all the boards of the tabernacle.

blocks.html: Put two tenons in each board.

items.html: And thou shalt make the boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards on the south side southward.

blocks.html: Make twenty boards for the south side of the tabernacle.

items.html: And thou shalt make forty sockets of silver under the twenty boards; two sockets under one board for his two tenons, and two sockets under another board for his two tenons.

blocks.html: Make forty silver sockets and put them under the twenty boards, two sockets and two tenons for each board.

items.html: And for the second side of the tabernacle on the north side there shall be twenty boards:
And their forty sockets of silver; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.

blocks.html: The north side shall also have twenty boards, with forty silver sockets, two sockets under each board.

items.html: And for the sides of the tabernacle westward thou shalt make six boards.

blocks.html: The west side shall have six boards.

items.html: And two boards shalt thou make for the corners of the tabernacle in the two sides.
And they shall be coupled together beneath, and they shall be coupled together above the head of it unto one ring: thus shall it be for them both; they shall be for the two corners.

blocks.html: Put two boards in the corners of the tabernacle, coupled together with a ring.

items.html: And they shall be eight boards, and their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.

blocks.html: There will be eight boards with sixteen silver sockets, two sockets under each board.

items.html: And thou shalt make bars of shittim wood; five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
And five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the side of the tabernacle, for the two sides westward.
And the middle bar in the midst of the boards shall reach from end to end.

blocks.html: Make bars of shittim wood, five for the boards on each side of the tabernacle, with the middle bar reaching end to end.

items.html: And thou shalt overlay the boards with gold, and make their rings of gold for places for the bars: and thou shalt overlay the bars with gold.

blocks.html: Overlay the boards with gold, and make rings of gold for the bars, which will also be overlayed with gold.

items.html: And thou shalt rear up the tabernacle according to the fashion thereof which was shewed thee in the mount.

blocks.html: Make all these things in the style I showed you on the mount.

items.html: And thou shalt make a vail of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen of cunning work: with cherubims shall it be made:

blocks.html: Make a blue, purple, and scarlet veil of cunning work with fine linen and cherubim.

items.html: And thou shalt hang it upon four pillars of shittim wood overlaid with gold: their hooks shall be of gold, upon the four sockets of silver.

blocks.html: Hang it on four shittim wood pillars overlaid with gold, with gold hooks and silver sockets.

items.html: And thou shalt hang up the vail under the taches, that thou mayest bring in thither within the vail the ark of the testimony: and the vail shall divide unto you between the holy place and the most holy.

blocks.html: Hang the veil under the taches.

items.html: And thou shalt put the mercy seat upon the ark of the testimony in the most holy place.

blocks.html: Put the mercy seat on the ark in the most holy place.

items.html: And thou shalt set the table without the vail, and the candlestick over against the table on the side of the tabernacle toward the south: and thou shalt put the table on the north side.

blocks.html: Set the table outside the veil, with the candlestick on the south and the table on the north.

items.html: And thou shalt make an hanging for the door of the tent, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, wrought with needlework.

blocks.html: Make a tent door hanging of blue, purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen.

items.html: And thou shalt make for the hanging five pillars of shittim wood, and overlay them with gold, and their hooks shall be of gold: and thou shalt cast five sockets of brass for them.

blocks.html: Make five shittim wood pillars, with gold hooks and five brass sockets.

footnotes.html:
Thou shalt make ... cherubims of cunning work. (v.1)

When Moses was up on Mount Sinai receiving the commandments from God, he also received instructions on making curtains, boards, bars, sockets, and rings.

Is it OK to make images?

blocks.html: How to make an altar and tabernacle court

items.html: And thou shalt make an altar of shittim wood, five cubits long, and five cubits broad; the altar shall be foursquare: and the height thereof shall be three cubits.

blocks.html:
God continues his instructions to Moses, saying,
Make an altar of shittim wood, five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high.

items.html: And thou shalt make the horns of it upon the four corners thereof: his horns shall be of the same: and thou shalt overlay it with brass.

blocks.html: Put horns in the four corners, overlayed with brass.

items.html: And thou shalt make his pans to receive his ashes, and his shovels, and his basons, and his fleshhooks, and his firepans: all the vessels thereof

blocks.html: Make pans for the ashes, shovels, basons, fleshhooks, and firepans.

items.html: And thou shalt make for it a grate of network of brass; and upon the net shalt thou make four brasen rings in the four corners thereof.

blocks.html: Make a brass grate with four brass rings in the four corners.

items.html: And thou shalt put it under the compass of the altar beneath, that the net may be even to the midst of the altar.

blocks.html: Put it under the compass of the altar.

items.html: And thou shalt make staves for the altar, staves of shittim wood, and overlay them with brass.

blocks.html: Make staves for the altar out of shittim wood and overlay them with brass.

items.html: And the staves shall be put into the rings, and the staves shall be upon the two sides of the altar, to bear it.

blocks.html: Put the staves into rings on two sides of the altar.

items.html: Hollow with boards shalt thou make it: as it was shewed thee in the mount, so shall they make it.

blocks.html: Make it hollow with boards, like I showed you on Mount Sinai.

items.html: And thou shalt make the court of the tabernacle: for the south side southward there shall be hangings for the court of fine twined linen of an hundred cubits long for one side:

blocks.html: Make the court of the tabernacle, with linen hangings on the south side one hundred cubits long.

items.html: And the twenty pillars thereof and their twenty sockets shall be of brass;

blocks.html: Make twenty pillars with twenty brass sockets.

items.html: And likewise for the north side in length there shall be hangings of an hundred cubits long, and his twenty pillars and their twenty sockets of brass; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets of silver.

blocks.html: Do the same on the north side (with hangings one hundred cubits long, twenty pillars, and sockets). Add hooks on the pillars with fillets of silver.

items.html: And for the breadth of the court on the west side shall be hangings of fifty cubits: their pillars ten, and their sockets ten.

blocks.html: Make fifty cubit hangings on the west side, with ten pillars and ten sockets.

items.html: And the breadth of the court on the east side eastward shall be fifty cubits.

blocks.html: The court on the east side shall also be fifty cubits.

items.html: The hangings of one side of the gate shall be fifteen cubits: their pillars three, and their sockets three.
And on the other side shall be hangings fifteen cubits: their pillars three, and their sockets three.

blocks.html: Make the hangings fifteen cubits on each side of the gate, with three pillars and three sockets.

items.html: And for the gate of the court shall be an hanging of twenty cubits, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, wrought with needlework: and their pillars shall be four, and their sockets four.

blocks.html: For the gate, make a blue, purple, and scarlet hanging twenty cubits long, with needleworrk, four pillars, and four sockets.

items.html: All the pillars round about the court shall be filleted with silver; their hooks shall be of silver, and their sockets of brass.

blocks.html: Cover the court pillars with silver, with hooks of silver and sockets of brass.

items.html: The length of the court shall be an hundred cubits, and the breadth fifty every where, and the height five cubits of fine twined linen, and their sockets of brass.

blocks.html: The length of the court shall be one hundred cubits, the width fifty cubits, and the height five cubits, with fine linen and sockets of brass.

items.html: All the vessels of the tabernacle in all the service thereof, and all the pins thereof, and all the pins of the court, shall be of brass.

blocks.html: All the tabernacle vessels and pins must be made of brass.

items.html: And thou shalt command the children of Israel, that they bring thee pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamp to burn always.

blocks.html: The people must bring pure olive oil to keep the lamp forever burning.

items.html: In the tabernacle of the congregation without the vail, which is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall order it from evening to morning before the LORD: it shall be a statute for ever unto their generations on the behalf of the children of Israel.

blocks.html: It shall be a statute forever.
How to make holy garments for priests
28:1-43, Cf. 1

items.html: And take thou unto thee Aaron thy brother, and his sons with him, from among the children of Israel, that he may minister unto me in the priest's office, even Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's sons.

blocks.html:
God continues his instructions to Moses, saying,
Make Aaron and his sons (Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar) priests, so they can serve me.

items.html: And thou shalt make holy garments for Aaron thy brother for glory and for beauty.

And thou shalt speak unto all that are wise hearted, whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom, that they may make Aaron's garments to consecrate him, that he may minister unto me in the priest's office.

blocks.html: And make holy garments for them for glory and beauty.

items.html: And these are the garments which they shall make; a breastplate, and an ephod, and a robe, and a broidered coat, a mitre, and a girdle: and they shall make holy garments for Aaron thy brother, and his sons, that he may minister unto me in the priest's office.
And they shall take gold, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen.

blocks.html: These are the garments that you shall make: a breastplate, an ephod, a robe, a broidered coat, a mitre, and a girdle.

items.html: And they shall make the ephod of gold, of blue, and of purple, of scarlet, and fine twined linen, with cunning work.

blocks.html: The ephod must be gold, blue, purple, and scarlet. Use fine twined linen, with cunning work.

items.html: It shall have the two shoulderpieces thereof joined at the two edges thereof; and so it shall be joined together.

blocks.html: Join the shoulderpieces together.

items.html: And the curious girdle of the ephod, which is upon it, shall be of the same, according to the work thereof; even of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen.

blocks.html: Make the curious girdle of the ephod in a similar manner, of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet, with fine twined linen.

items.html: And thou shalt take two onyx stones, and grave on them the names of the children of Israel:
Six of their names on one stone, and the other six names of the rest on the other stone, according to their birth.
With the work of an engraver in stone, like the engravings of a signet, shalt thou engrave the two stones with the names of the children of Israel: thou shalt make them to be set in ouches of gold.

blocks.html: Take two onyx stones and engrave in gold the names of the twelve sons of Israel, six on one stone and six on another.

items.html: And thou shalt put the two stones upon the shoulders of the ephod for stones of memorial unto the children of Israel: and Aaron shall bear their names before the LORD upon his two shoulders for a memorial.
And thou shalt make ouches of gold;
And two chains of pure gold at the ends; of wreathen work shalt thou make them, and fasten the wreathen chains to the ouches.

blocks.html: Put the two stones on the shoulders of the ephod, with two gold chains at the ends.

items.html: And thou shalt make the breastplate of judgment with cunning work; after the work of the ephod thou shalt make it; of gold, of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, and of fine twined linen, shalt thou make it.
Foursquare it shall be being doubled; a span shall be the length thereof, and a span shall be the breadth thereof.

blocks.html:
Make the breastplate of cunning work from fine linen, of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet.

It must be square, a span and a half on each side.

items.html: And thou shalt set in it settings of stones, even four rows of stones: the first row shall be a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle: this shall be the first row.

blocks.html: Set the breastplate in four rows of stones; the first row shall be a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle.

items.html: And the second row shall be an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond.

blocks.html: The second row: an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond.

items.html: And the third row a ligure, an agate, and an amethyst.

blocks.html: The third row: a ligure, an agate, and an amethyst.

items.html: And the fourth row a beryl, and an onyx, and a jasper: they shall be set in gold in their inclosings.

blocks.html: And the fourth row: a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper.

items.html: And the stones shall be with the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names, like the engravings of a signet; every one with his name shall they be according to the twelve tribes.

blocks.html: Each stone shall have the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

items.html: And thou shalt make upon the breastplate chains at the ends of wreathen work of pure gold.
And thou shalt make upon the breastplate two rings of gold, and shalt put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate.
And thou shalt put the two wreathen chains of gold in the two rings which are on the ends of the breastplate.
And the other two ends of the two wreathen chains thou shalt fasten in the two ouches, and put them on the shoulderpieces of the ephod before it.

blocks.html:
Put chains on the breastplate at the ends of the wreathen work of pure gold.

One end of the chains will be put through two gold rings at the end of the breastplate.

Fasten the other ends of the chain to the shoulderpieces of the ephod.

items.html: And thou shalt make two rings of gold, and thou shalt put them upon the two ends of the breastplate in the border thereof, which is in the side of the ephod inward.

blocks.html: Make two gold rings and put them on the ends of the breastplate next to the inner part of the ephod.

items.html: And two other rings of gold thou shalt make, and shalt put them on the two sides of the ephod underneath, toward the forepart thereof, over against the the other coupling therof, above the curious girdle of the ephod.

blocks.html: Put two gold rings underneath the ephod, toward the front, near the coupling, above the curious girdle of the ephod.

items.html: And they shall bind the breastplate by the rings thereof unto the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, that it may be above the curious girdle of the ephod, and that the breastplate be not loosed from the ephod.

blocks.html: Bind the breastplate by the rings to the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, so it will be above the curious girdle of the ephod.

items.html: And Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastplate of judgment upon his heart, when he goeth in unto the holy place, for a memorial before the LORD continually.

And thou shalt put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim; and they shall be upon Aaron's heart, when he goeth in before the LORD: and Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart before the LORD continually.

blocks.html: Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel on the breastplate of judgment on his heart, along with 2, when he goes into the holy place.

items.html: And thou shalt make the robe of the ephod all of blue.
And there shall be an hole in the top of it, in the midst thereof: it shall have a binding of woven work round about the hole of it, as it were the hole of an habergeon, that it be not rent.

blocks.html: Make a blue robe with a hole in the top, with a binding so it won't tear.

items.html: And beneath upon the hem of it thou shalt make pomegranates of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, round about the hem thereof; and bells of gold between them round about:
A golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, upon the hem of the robe round about.

blocks.html: Make a hem of blue, purple, and scarlet pomegranates, with gold bells between them.

items.html: And it shall be upon Aaron to minister: and his sound shall be heard when he goeth in unto the holy place before the LORD, and when he cometh out, that he die not.

blocks.html: Aaron must sound his bell when he goes into the holy place - or die.

items.html: And thou shalt make a plate of pure gold, and grave upon it, like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD.
And thou shalt put it on a blue lace, that it may be upon the mitre; upon the forefront of the mitre it shall be.

And it shall be upon Aaron's forehead, that Aaron may bear the iniquity of the holy things, which the children of Israel shall hallow in all their holy gifts; and it shall be always upon his forehead, that they may be accepted before the LORD.

blocks.html:
Make a plate of pure gold and engrave these words upon it: HOLINESS TO THE LORD.

Set the plate on blue lace and put it on the front of Aaron's mitre.

This plate must always be on Aaron's forehead, since he bears the iniquity of the holy things.

items.html: And thou shalt embroider the coat of fine linen, and thou shalt make the mitre of fine linen, and thou shalt make the girdle of needlework.

blocks.html: Make the mitre and embroider the coat with fine linen. And make the girdle of needlework.

items.html: And for Aaron's sons thou shalt make coats, and thou shalt make for them girdles, and bonnets shalt thou make for them, for glory and for beauty.
And thou shalt put them upon Aaron thy brother, and his sons with him; and shalt anoint them, and consecrate them, and sanctify them, that they may minister unto me in the priest's office.

blocks.html: Make coats, girdles, and bonnets for Aaron's sons for glory and beauty.

items.html: And thou shalt make them linen breeches to cover their nakedness; from the loins even unto the thighs they shall reach:

blocks.html: Make linen breeches for Aaron and his sons to cover their nakedness, reaching from their loins to their thighs.

items.html: And they shall be upon Aaron, and upon his sons, when they come in unto the tabernacle of the congregation, or when they come near unto the altar to minister in the holy place; that they bear not iniquity, and die: it shall be a statute for ever unto him and his seed after him.

blocks.html:
If they come into the holy place without their holy breeches on, they will die.

This shall be a statute forever.
The procedure for making priests
29:1-21, Cf. Lev 8:1-36

items.html: And this is the thing that thou shalt do unto them to hallow them, to minister unto me in the priest's office: Take one young bullock, and two rams without blemish,

blocks.html:
God continues his instructions to Moses, saying,

This is the thing you must do to make priests holy ministers to me:

Take one young bullock and two unblemished rams.

items.html: And unleavened bread, and cakes unleavened tempered with oil, and wafers unleavened anointed with oil: of wheaten flour shalt thou make them.

blocks.html: Put some unleavened bread, oiled cakes and wafers in a basket.

items.html: And thou shalt put them into one basket, and bring them in the basket, with the bullock and the two rams.
And Aaron and his sons thou shalt bring unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and shalt wash them with water.

blocks.html: Bring them to the door of the tabernacle, where Aaron and his sons will wash them with water.

items.html: And thou shalt take the garments, and put upon Aaron the coat, and the robe of the ephod, and the ephod, and the breastplate, and gird him with the curious girdle of the ephod:

blocks.html: Put these garments on Aaron: the coat, robe, ephod, breastplate, and curious girdle of the ephod.

items.html: And thou shalt put the mitre upon his head, and put the holy crown upon the mitre.

blocks.html: Put the mitre on his head, and the holy crown on the mitre.

items.html: Then shalt thou take the anointing oil, and pour it upon his head, and anoint him.

blocks.html: Pour anointing oil on his head.

items.html: And thou shalt bring his sons, and put coats upon them.
And thou shalt gird them with girdles, Aaron and his sons, and put the bonnets on them: and the priest's office shall be theirs for a perpetual statute: and thou shalt consecrate Aaron and his sons.

blocks.html: Bring Aaron's sons and put coats on them, gird them with girdles, and put bonnets on them.

items.html: And thou shalt cause a bullock to be brought before the tabernacle of the congregation: and Aaron and his sons shall put their hands upon the head of the bullock.

blocks.html: Bring the bullock to the tabernacle, where Aaron and his sons will put their hands on its head.

items.html: And thou shalt kill the bullock before the LORD, by the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.

blocks.html: Kill the bullock in front of God, by the door of the tabernacle. [1]

items.html: And thou shalt take of the blood of the bullock, and put it upon the horns of the altar with thy finger, and pour all the blood beside the bottom of the altar.

blocks.html: Wipe the bullock's blood on the horns of the altar with your finger, and pour the remaining blood at the bottom of the altar.

items.html: And thou shalt take all the fat that covereth the inwards, and the caul that is above the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and burn them upon the altar.

blocks.html: Take the fat and kidneys and burn them on the altar.

items.html: But the flesh of the bullock, and his skin, and his dung, shalt thou burn with fire without the camp: it is a sin offering.
Thou shalt also take one ram; and Aaron and his sons shall put their hands upon the head of the ram.

blocks.html: Burn the flesh, skin, and dung outside the camp for a sin offering.

items.html: And thou shalt slay the ram, and thou shalt take his blood, and sprinkle it round about upon the altar.

blocks.html: Also kill the ram and take its blood and sprinkle it round about the altar.

items.html: And thou shalt cut the ram in pieces, and wash the inwards of him, and his legs, and put them unto his pieces, and unto his head.

blocks.html: Cut the ram in pieces, and wash the internal organs, legs, and head.

items.html: And thou shalt burn the whole ram upon the altar: it is a burnt offering unto the LORD: it is a sweet savour, an offering made by fire unto the LORD.

blocks.html:
Burn the ram on the altar for a burnt offering to me.

It is a sweet savor to me.

items.html: And thou shalt take the other ram; and Aaron and his sons shall put their hands upon the head of the ram.

blocks.html: Have Aaron and his sons put their hands on the other ram.

items.html: Then shalt thou kill the ram, and take of his blood, and put it upon the tip of the right ear of Aaron, and upon the tip of the right ear of his sons, and upon the thumb of their right hand, and upon the great toe of their right foot, and sprinkle the blood upon the altar round about.

blocks.html:
Kill the ram and wipe some of its blood on Aaron's right ear, thumb, and big toe.

Sprinkle the remaining blood on the altar round about.

items.html: And thou shalt take of the blood that is upon the altar, and of the anointing oil, and sprinkle it upon Aaron, and upon his garments, and upon his sons, and upon the garments of his sons with him: and he shall be hallowed, and his garments, and his sons, and his sons' garments with him.

blocks.html:
Take the blood that is on the altar and spinkle it on Aaron and his sons and on their garments.

This will make them and their garments holy.
Wave, heave, and sin offerings

The gold of the offering, was twenty and nine talents, and seven hundred and thirty shekels. (v.24)

A group of Hebrew slaves carried 1000 kg of gold, 3500 kg of silver, and 2450 kg of brass with them as they traveled through the wilderness. (And this was after they used all their gold to make a golden calf.) This amount of gold and silver would be worth more than $40 million US dollars today.

Six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty men (v.26)

Seventy people (Gen 46:27, Ex 1:5) became several million (603,550 men and a couple million women and children) in 400 years (Gen 15:13).

items.html: And thou shalt set up the court round about, and hang up the hanging at the court gate.

blocks.html: Set up the court and hang the hangings at the gate.

items.html: And thou shalt take the anointing oil, and anoint the tabernacle, and all that is therein, and shalt hallow it, and all the vessels thereof: and it shall be holy.

blocks.html: Anoint the tabernacle and vessels with the anointing oil. It will all be holy.

items.html: And thou shalt anoint the altar of the burnt offering, and all his vessels, and sanctify the altar: and it shall be an altar most holy.

blocks.html: Anoint the altar of the burnt offering, with its vessels. It will be most holy.

items.html: And thou shalt anoint the laver and his foot, and sanctify it.

blocks.html: Anoint the laver and its foot.

items.html: And thou shalt bring Aaron and his sons unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and wash them with water.

blocks.html: Bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the tabernacle, and wash them with water.

items.html: And thou shalt put upon Aaron the holy garments, and anoint him, and sanctify him; that he may minister unto me in the priest's office.

blocks.html: Put the holy garments on Aaron and anoint him, so he can minister to me as a priest.

items.html: And thou shalt bring his sons, and clothe them with coats:

And thou shalt anoint them, as thou didst anoint their father, that they may minister unto me in the priest's office: for their anointing shall surely be an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.

blocks.html:
Bring his sons, put coats on them, and anoint them like you did their father, so they can minister to me as priests.

It will be a lasting priesthood, throughout their generations.

items.html: Thus did Moses: according to all that the LORD commanded him, so did he.

blocks.html: Moses did everything God commanded.

items.html: And it came to pass in the first month in the second year, on the first day of the month, that the tabernacle was reared up.

blocks.html: The tabernacle was erected on first day of the first month of the second year.

items.html: And Moses reared up the tabernacle, and fastened his sockets, and set up the boards thereof, and put in the bars thereof, and reared up his pillars.

blocks.html: Moses fastened the sockets, set up the boards, put in the bars, and erected the pillars.

items.html: And he spread abroad the tent over the tabernacle, and put the covering of the tent above upon it; as the LORD commanded Moses.

blocks.html: He put up the tent and its covering, as God commanded.

items.html: And he took and put the testimony into the ark, and set the staves on the ark, and put the mercy seat above upon the ark:

blocks.html: He put the testimomy in the ark, set the staves, and put the mercy seat above the ark.

items.html: And he brought the ark into the tabernacle, and set up the vail of the covering, and covered the ark of the testimony; as the LORD commanded Moses.

blocks.html: He brought the ark into the tabernacle, set up the veil, and covered the ark, as God comanded.

items.html: And he put the table in the tent of the congregation, upon the side of the tabernacle northward, without the vail.

blocks.html: He put the table in the tent, on the north side, outside the wall.

items.html: And he set the bread in order upon it before the LORD; as the LORD had commanded Moses.

blocks.html: He set the bread on the table in front of God, as God commanded.

items.html: And he put the candlestick in the tent of the congregation, over against the table, on the side of the tabernacle southward.

blocks.html: He put the candlestick in the tent, against the table, on the south side of the tabernacle.

items.html: And he lighted the lamps before the LORD; as the LORD commanded Moses.

blocks.html: He lighted the lamps in front of God, as God commanded.

items.html: And he put the golden altar in the tent of the congregation before the vail:

blocks.html: He put the golden altar in the tent in front of the veil.

items.html: And he burnt sweet incense thereon; as the LORD commanded Moses.

blocks.html: He burned sweet incense on the altar, as God commanded.

items.html: And he set up the hanging at the door of the tabernacle.

blocks.html: He set up the hanging at the door of the tabernacle.

items.html: And he put the altar of burnt offering by the door of the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation, and offered upon it the burnt offering and the meat offering; as the LORD commanded Moses.

blocks.html: He put the burnt offering altar by the door of the tabernacle, and offered the burnt offering and the meat offering, as God commanded.

items.html: And he set the laver between the tent of the congregation and the altar, and put water there, to wash withal.

blocks.html: He set up the bowl and put water in it.

items.html: And Moses and Aaron and his sons washed their hands and their feet thereat:

blocks.html: And Moses and Aaron washed their hands and feet in it.

items.html: When they went into the tent of the congregation, and when they came near unto the altar, they washed; as the LORD commanded Moses.

blocks.html: Whenever they came into the tent or came near the altar, they washed, as God commanded.

items.html: And he reared up the court round about the tabernacle and the altar, and set up the hanging of the court gate. So Moses finished the work.

blocks.html:
Moses set up the court around the tabernacle and the altar, and set up the hanging of the court gate.

And Moses finished his work.
A cloud at night and a fire during the day

items.html: Then a cloud covered the tent of the congregation, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
And Moses was not able to enter into the tent of the congregation, because the cloud abode thereon, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.

blocks.html: A cloud covered the tent and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle.

items.html: And when the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel went onward in all their journeys:
But if the cloud were not taken up, then they journeyed not till the day that it was taken up.

blocks.html:
When the cloud was over the tent, the people stayed where they were.

Whenever the cloud left, the people went on with their journey.

items.html: For the cloud of the LORD was upon the tabernacle by day, and fire was on it by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.

blocks.html: The cloud of the Lord stayed on the tabernacle during the day, with a fire on it at night. [1]

footnotes.html:
When the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel went onward in all their journeys. (v.38)

The cloud of the LORD was upon the tabernacle by day ... throughout all their journeys.

Since the Israelites didn't travel if the cloud stayed on the tabernacle, and the cloud stayed on the tabernacle thoughout their journey, I guess they never made it to the promised land. Oh well....
